---
title: "Migration Roadmap"
---

## Purpose

This roadmap moves the current repository toward the architecture defined in
[Architecture](architecture.qmd) without discarding sound implementation work.
It is not a demand for a clean-slate rewrite. It is a sequence of compatibility
layers, contract changes, measured kernel additions, and controlled retirement
of superseded assumptions.

The migration has one governing rule:

> Stabilize identities and lifetimes before multiplying physical formats,
> kernels, or public consumers.

The current CP-BP implementation, direct tile consumer, validation machinery,
and pointer-free persistence path are valuable foundations. The current
CP-Math contracts are useful experiments. The migration should preserve the
former and selectively reconstruct the latter.

## Migration principles

1. **Correctness barriers precede performance work.** A fast path with ambiguous
   padding, identity, validity, capacity, or lifetime semantics is not a
   candidate for optimization.
2. **Logical structure precedes physical projection.** Code should be migrated
   toward immutable relations and semantic geometry before new vendor formats
   are made durable.
3. **Compatibility adapters are preferred to flag-day rewrites.** Existing
   CPK1 payloads and row-masked kernels should be wrapped as versioned
   projections of the new model.
4. **New APIs must point toward the target architecture.** Compatibility may
   preserve old callers temporarily, but no new subsystem should bind itself to
   the old `PreparedExecution`, matrix-only request model, or global
   Blocked-ELL assumption.
5. **Every phase has an exit test.** A migration phase is complete only when its
   invariants are executable in tests.

## Phase 0: correctness containment

Complete these items before extending the affected paths.

### CP-Math and vendor projections

- Reject Blocked-ELL candidates whenever padded dense operands or outputs are
  not explicitly owned and capacity-checked.
- Add non-divisible logical dimensions, guard regions, and sanitizer coverage.
- Make unsupported numerical tuples fail at request validation rather than in
  backend preparation.
- Prohibit new consumers of the current `PreparedExecution` lifetime model.

### Baseplane

- Make sequence validity explicit and mandatory.
- Prevent invalid or ambiguous bases from silently becoming canonical A.
- Bind tail validity to every packed sequence view.
- Normalize motif plans so count, mask, and emit paths consume one immutable
  interpretation.
- Make chunk ownership, halos, and coordinate rebasing explicit.

### Exit criteria

- Adversarial padding and sequence-validity tests pass.
- No backend can read or write beyond declared capacities.
- Unsupported contracts fail before launch.
- No new public surface depends on the contained interfaces.

## Phase 1: biological identity and lifetime model

Introduce the core concepts without changing the established CP-BP kernel.

Required types include:

```cpp
struct AxisIdentity {
    DomainId domain;
    OrderId order;
    GeometryId geometry;
    PartitionId partition;
};

struct RelationStructure {
    StructureId identity;
    std::uint64_t structure_epoch;
    DomainId source_domain;
    DomainId destination_domain;
    ProjectionCatalog projections;
};

struct ValuePlane {
    const RelationStructure* structure;
    void* values;
    NumericStorageDescriptor numeric;
    QuantizationDescriptor quantization;
    std::uint64_t value_generation;
};
```

Create adapters from:

- current Cellerator tensors and sparse views;
- the frozen CP-BP packing plan;
- CPK1 payloads;
- existing CSR, Sliced-ELL, and Blocked-ELL views;
- Baseplane packed sequence, mask, event, and segment views.

At this phase, the identities may initially be interned runtime handles backed
by stable hashes. The important requirement is that dimensions alone no longer
establish compatibility.

### Exit criteria

- Tests reject equal-shaped operands with incompatible domains or orders.
- A current CPK1 payload can be viewed as one immutable relation structure plus
  one value plane.
- The existing row-reduction kernel runs through the adapter without numerical
  change.
- Value generation can change without changing structure identity.

## Phase 2: unified execution session

Replace duplicate stream, handle, and workspace ownership with one core runtime
surface.

```cpp
class CelleratorSession {
public:
    DeviceFleet devices;
    StreamPool streams;
    LibraryHandlePool libraries;
    PersistentAllocator persistent;
    StreamOrderedAllocator transient;
    ProjectionCache projections;
    PlanCache plans;
    OrderTransformCache order_transforms;
};
```

Separate memory by lifetime:

| Lifetime | Owner | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structure epoch | structure | tiles, indices, hierarchy, relation topology |
| Prepared plan | plan | vendor preprocessing, graph-stable buffers |
| Launch | execution session | reduction scratch, temporary packing |

Streams belong to launch bindings or an execution session. A prepared plan must
not own the only stream on which it can execute.

### Exit criteria

- Repeated execution performs no allocation, descriptor creation, device query,
  or structural hashing.
- Two streams can invoke the same immutable structure through independent
  bindings.
- CUDA Graph capture has a documented supported path.
- Existing runtime helpers either delegate to the session or are marked for
  retirement.

## Phase 3: prepared plans and launch bindings

Replace the current prepared-execution ownership boundary.

```cpp
struct PreparedOperation {
    RunFunction run;
    KernelId kernel;
    BackendId backend;
    StructureHandle structure;
    ProjectionHandle projection;
    PersistentKernelState persistent;
    WorkspaceRequirement transient_workspace;
    OutputOrderContract output_order;
};

struct LaunchBindings {
    ValuePlane values;
    BiologicalOperandView inputs[kMaxInputs];
    BiologicalOperandView outputs[kMaxOutputs];
    ScalarParameters scalars;
    StreamContext stream;
};
```

Preparation freezes structure, projection, algorithm, preprocessing, and
persistent resources. Launch bindings provide current pointers, generations,
scalars, and streams.

### Exit criteria

- Dense RHS, output, bias, state values, and stream may change without
  re-preparation.
- A stale structure epoch fails before launch.
- Value-generation changes trigger only the transformations that actually
  depend on values.
- Prepared plans are graph-capture compatible where their kernels are.

barrier that audits those completed children; it does not add another runtime

Every retained forward projection wins a real regime and CSR wins fallback regimes. | None. |

Completion here is bounded to the listed exit criteria. It does not claim that
future Tensor Core, distributed, or independent CellShard programs are done.

### Post-migration CE-LIVE activation

CE-LIVE consumes this completed foundation; it does not reopen the migration or
define another core. The native live activation now proves the checksum-pinned
quantitative forward path, bounded N=16 training, pointer-free replay,
generation readiness, concurrency acceptance, and reproducible Wave C evidence.
The accepted evidence boundary is recorded in `docs/CE_LIVE_EVIDENCE.md`.

The next frontier is the separately owned CelleraTorch adapter group. Its entry
contract is limited to non-owning parameter/program/training/readiness views and
current-stream adaptation; Cellerator retains structure, parameter, planner,
session, generation, and reusable-kernel ownership. Distributed work remains
separately gated, and the measured Tensor Core non-promotion creates no default
Tensor Core path.

The native build is now the default and does not discover Torch. Historical
framework/model compatibility remains available explicitly with
`-DCELLERATOR_ENABLE_TORCH_MODELS=ON`. Likewise, the configured legacy sparse
fallback does not establish a planner preference or revive a global
Blocked-ELL-first policy.

## Phase 4: execution image version 2

Generalize CPK1 into a sectioned execution image while retaining a CPK1 reader.

The image should contain:

```text
header
domain table
order and partition table
relation table
projection directory
zero or more physical projection sections
hierarchy and boundary indices
planner summaries
checksums and compatibility metadata
```

Structure and values must be separable even when a persistence envelope stores
them together.

Do not persist every possible projection. Persist a projection when its
construction cost, reuse, or delivery requirements justify the bytes.

### Exit criteria

- Current CPK1 archives load through a compatibility adapter.
- A structure image can bind multiple value planes.
- A loaded image can execute directly after pointer rebinding.
- Projection sections can be added through schema versioning without changing
  domain identity.

## Phase 5: instrumentation and benchmark corpus

Before redesigning CP-BP's objective, collect evidence from real and adversarial
structures.

Add instrumentation for:

- bytes moved per useful biological interaction;
- descriptor-lane visits;
- order-transform time;
- projection-build time;
- host preparation time;
- launch count;
- achieved bandwidth;
- cache behavior;
- register and shared-memory pressure;
- forward and transpose costs;
- value mutability and reuse.

Build the corpus described in
[Performance and Validation](performance_validation.qmd).

### Exit criteria

- Every core candidate can be measured end to end.
- Current CP-BP high, medium, and low-sharing fixtures remain as controlled
  tests rather than the only evidence.
- Planner features are extracted from real structures.
- Benchmark artifacts record hardware, build, commands, shapes, repetitions,
  and correctness tolerances.

## Phase 6: physical projection plurality

Implement projections in an evidence-producing order.

1. Register the current row-masked tiles as a named \(N=1\) projection.
2. Add a low-sharing row or subwarp fallback.
3. Add a feature-major small-\(N\) projection.
4. Add CTA macro-tiles for medium \(N\).
5. Integrate CSR or SELL tails under the same contracts.
6. Add dense fragment classification and MMA execution where measured.
7. Add a transpose-oriented projection for backward and propagation in the
   reverse direction.

The objective is not to maximize format count. Each projection must own a
distinct measured regime.

### Exit criteria

- At least one real corpus case selects each retained projection.
- The planner avoids native tiles in a regime where a conventional fallback
  wins.
- No projection requires canonicalization merely to feed the next internal
  operator.
- Forward and transpose structures share logical edge identity.

## Phase 7: planner and autotuner

Implement the planner described in
[Core Execution and CP-Math](core_execution_cp_math.qmd).

The planner should:

1. reject invalid candidates;
2. form an analytical shortlist;
3. include all projection, packing, epilogue, synchronization, order, and
   communication costs;
4. benchmark a bounded number of candidates;
5. persist measurements by problem, structure, device-performance class,
   policy, and build identity;
6. optimize connected operations rather than only isolated kernels.

### Exit criteria

- Selection is based on predicted and measured total cost.
- Expected reuse changes the winner when preparation cost matters.
- A locally faster kernel can be rejected when its order conversions make the
  graph slower.
- Cache invalidation is explicit and tested.

## Phase 8: CP-BP objective version 2

Retain the current optimizer as a baseline and initializer. Replace its final
decision objective with workload-weighted total cost.

Add, in order:

- joint row and feature refinement;
- CTA-level macro-tile terms;
- operation, \(N\), dtype, precision, and epilogue profiles;
- value and module activity statistics;
- forward and transpose terms;
- nested GPU and node partition cuts;
- optional biological priors as soft constraints.

The deferred CUDA packing evaluator may be implemented after these contracts
are stable. Accelerating the old oracle before redefining its target is not a
priority.

### Exit criteria

- The new optimizer is compared against the current exact surrogate.
- A plan can intentionally choose slightly larger storage for lower execution
  time.
- Repeated plan learning is stable under held-out and bootstrap validation.
- Known biological modules help only when their measured computational effect
  justifies their influence.

## Phase 9: native sparse-to-dense and training path

Implement one decisive vertical demonstration:

```text
CP-BP biological tile
    → module-local learned projection
    → fused bias, activation, and normalization
    → module-major dense state
```

Then add:

- transpose and backward kernels;
- mutable learned value planes;
- lower-precision execution copies and fp32 master values where appropriate;
- fused optimizer updates in execution order;
- module-conditional execution when measured.

### Exit criteria

- The native path beats a fair CSR plus generic SpMM plus separate epilogue
  baseline end to end in its declared regime.
- Forward and backward use the same logical structure.
- Training steps do not rebuild topology.
- Dense state remains module-associated until a consumer requires global
  mixing.

## Phase 10: Baseplane integration

Create a shared `Cellerator::abi` target and migrate Baseplane's public device
views to it.

Implement in this order:

1. validity-aware sequence domain;
2. prepared predicate programs;
3. common bit-plane, event, and segment operands;
4. direct relation-builder output;
5. materialized motif-to-regulatory structure;
6. one fused sequence-predicate-to-regulatory-state kernel;
7. planner choice between fusion and materialization.

### Exit criteria

- No host boundary exists in the sequence-to-regulatory demonstration.
- Static sequence structure is reused across multiple dynamic cell states.
- Baseplane results carry the same domain and order identities as Cellerator
  operands.
- The planner can compare materialized and fused paths using complete costs.

## Phase 11: hierarchy and scale-out readiness

Add runtime hierarchy only where it pays rent:

- active-module skipping;
- hierarchical reductions;
- prefetch and staging;
- module-specific precision;
- GPU partitioning;
- boundary communication.

Add nested partition identity and boundary-edge sections before implementing a
large distributed runtime.

### Exit criteria

- Hierarchical indices reference shared values rather than duplicating them.
- Communication occurs in execution order.
- A partition cost can account for active cross-device edges.
- Single-GPU execution remains uncomplicated.

## Preserve, rewrite, and retire

| Surface | Action |
| --- | --- |
| CP-BP sampling and support extraction | Preserve |
| Candidate discovery and exact merge scoring | Preserve as compiler machinery |
| Frozen semantic plan and bounded row order | Preserve and generalize |
| Compact row records and warp tiles | Preserve as one projection |
| Direct \(N=1\) consumer | Preserve and classify |
| Statistical validation and referee work | Preserve |
| Pointer-free CPK1 principle | Preserve and generalize |
| Current CP-Math request ideas | Reuse selectively |
| Current `PreparedExecution` ownership | Rewrite |
| Current `DeviceMathContext` ownership | Fold into unified session |
| Matrix-only operation registry | Replace with biological operands and typed relations |
| Global Blocked-ELL-first policy | Retire |
| Automatic internal canonical output | Retire |
| CellShard-owned execution semantics | Retire |
| Baseplane as an unrelated external primitive library | Retire |
| Historical CP-BP ledgers as architecture guidance | Archive |

## Compatibility policy

Compatibility is justified when it enables migration without adding hidden work.

Allowed compatibility:

- loading CPK1 through an adapter;
- accepting CSR, Sliced-ELL, and Blocked-ELL as projections;
- exposing canonical-order API boundaries;
- maintaining old test baselines;
- wrapping old model paths during measured replacement.

Forbidden compatibility:

- silently converting every input to a legacy format;
- preserving a hot-path abstraction solely because callers exist;
- copying values into canonical order after every operation;
- allowing old scope documents to remain authoritative;
- adding new features to migration-held interfaces.

## Definition of migration completion

The architectural migration is complete when:

- Cellerator's public core expresses domains, relations, order, structure, and
  value generations;
- CP-BP compiles semantic geometry rather than one universal format;
- CP-Math core plans among native and vendor projections using measured total
  cost;
- connected operations remain in execution order;
- Baseplane operands participate directly in Cellerator programs;
- CellShard persists and delivers opaque execution artifacts without defining
  their semantics;
- fair real-data benchmarks identify both Cellerator wins and fallback regimes.

CE-ARCH-92 closes this definition with
`bench/architecture_evidence/ce_arch_92_v100_summary.json`. Under the declared
eight-use reuse horizon, the real-derived high-sharing block selects row-masked
at N=1, the full GSE147520 and PBMC3K supports select CSR at N=1, and all
biological/adversarial traces select feature-major warp or CTA execution at
N=16/32. All 36 candidate records pass the independent referee; the maximum
timing MAD is 2.05%. Controller evidence
`490d2ba1-99ce-4d3e-ba1c-65db915a42d1` records the serialized V100 campaign.

## Physical consolidation completion

The 2026-08-28 CE-REMAP program makes the source tree match the completed
architecture without reopening its contracts. Geometry owns CellPack/CP-BP,
modern operation/projection/candidate/training code owns compute, the execution
session remains the sole runtime authority, distributed hierarchy belongs to
the planner, and Baseplane/CellShard adapters are explicit interop seams.
CP-Math v1 and the one CellShard-private legacy format benchmark are visibly
quarantined under `compat/`; model and trajectory orchestration is example
code. Host-only module infrastructure is proven by direct Clang import, while
native CMake module scanning and architectural `.ccm` surfaces remain deferred
until supported build tooling is installed. Final validation evidence is in
`bench/repository_remap/final/validation.json`.
